CC BY permits redistribution, so the PDF is archived. EXTRACTION -- markitdown. This is a Frontiers two-column layout and the conversion is the worst in this batch: the two columns are interleaved line by line, so a sentence from the left column is followed by an unrelated sentence from the right, and much of the running text is additionally wrapped inside spurious empty markdown tables. Words also lose inter-word spacing in places ('thedownstreamdatasets'). md_quality: rough. Specifically usable: Table 1 (downstream dataset summary) and Table 2 (best performance per dataset) survive as legible rows and are the source of the 86.7 / 42.6 / 0.65 / 0.72 / 0.72 figures and of the sampling rates and channel counts. Specifically unusable: Figure 5, which is the only place the six fine-tuning configurations are compared numerically, is a violin plot and yields nothing but its caption; the caption's qualitative statements are what the card quotes. Figures 1-4 likewise yield only captions. VERIFICATION AGAINST THE PDF -- the transformer's feed-forward dimension was re-read directly from page 6 of the PDF with pypdf because 3076 looked like a conversion error next to a model dimension of 1536; the PDF prints 'internal feed-forward dimension of 3076', so the value is the paper's, not the converter's, and the card says so. The 'total hours not reported' claim was checked with a Python substring count rather than grep, per collection practice: 'hour' and 'Hour' each occur zero times in source.md, and the corpus is described only in terabytes and subject counts.
